purpose: Hydrocortisone butyrate is a cream, ointment, or lotion you put on your skin to relieve redness, itching, and swelling caused by certain skin conditions. It is commonly used for eczema, dermatitis, psoriasis, and other inflammatory skin problems. It helps make your skin feel more comfortable and look less irritated.
how_it_works: This medicine contains a mild steroid that calms down the immune response happening in your skin. Think of it like turning down the volume on your skin's inflammation — it reduces the chemicals in your body that cause redness, swelling, and itching. It does not cure the underlying condition, but it gives your skin relief while it heals.
common_side_effects: Mild burning, stinging, or itching when you first apply it. You may notice some dryness, irritation, or skin thinning with long-term use. Some people notice a slight lightening of the skin in the area where it is applied.
warnings: Do not use this on your face, underarms, or groin unless your doctor specifically tells you to, as skin there is more sensitive. Avoid using it on open wounds or infected skin. Do not wrap the treated area tightly with bandages unless directed by your doctor, as this can increase absorption. Keep it away from your eyes. Using it too long or on large areas can affect your body's natural hormone levels, so follow your doctor's instructions carefully.
typical_dosing: Apply a thin layer to the affected skin area 2 to 3 times a day, or as directed by your doctor. Gently rub it in until it disappears into the skin. Wash your hands before and after applying unless your hands are the area being treated. Use only as long as needed — most people use it for a short period of 2 to 4 weeks.
